title: What Happens When You Cry?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Lacrimal Apparatus' (lacrimal glands behind the upper outside corner of your eyes make the salty water that becomes your tears; every time you blink, your puncta act like valves that drain used tears away from your eye; your tear ducts empty into the back of your nose; when you cry, your excess tears are flowing faster than they usually would into the back of your nose and draining into your throat, which is why you might feel stuffy if you've been crying; page says 'stuffy', not 'runny'): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/24415-lacrimal-apparatus

Cleveland Clinic, 'Tears' (three types: basal tears keep your eyes lubricated, reflex tears flush out irritants like dust, smoke or onion fumes, and strong emotions like sadness, joy or grief cause emotional tears; tears drain into your tear ducts that empty into the back of your nose): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/tears

Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'Tears: Why We Cry and More (Infographic)' (emotional tears gush in response to strong emotions; they have the same chemical makeup as basal tears but contain more stress hormones and natural painkillers): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/tears-why-we-cry-and-more-infographic/

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Skin Flushing' (skin flushing, or blushing, is the sudden increase of blood flow to your cheeks, neck or upper chest, turning them red or darker temporarily; most often a reaction to strong emotions like affection or embarrassment; it goes away on its own): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/skin-flushing

lines.text: Your eyes flood, but the weirdest part happens in your nose.
lines.caps: YOUR EYES *FLOOD | BUT THE *WEIRDEST | PART *HAPPENS | IN YOUR *NOSE

lines.text: Tears come from glands behind the upper outside corner of each eye.
lines.caps: *TEARS COME FROM | *GLANDS BEHIND | THE UPPER *OUTSIDE | CORNER OF EACH *EYE

lines.text: Strong feelings like sadness or joy open the floodgates,
and those emotional tears carry extra stress hormones and natural painkillers.
lines.caps: AND THOSE *EMOTIONAL | TEARS *CARRY | EXTRA *STRESS | *HORMONES AND | NATURAL *PAINKILLERS

lines.text: Normally, every blink drains used tears into your tear ducts,
which empty into the back of your nose.
Cry, and tears rush in faster than usual,
then drain down into your throat.
That's why a good cry leaves you feeling stuffy.
lines.caps: THAT'S *WHY A GOOD | *CRY LEAVES YOU | FEELING *STUFFY
